Case expectations and accepted values are UNCHANGED from v1. v3 (same day, after live run 1): scorer-side extensions only — generalized unit-word measurement rule, echo-gap additive runs, currency-suffixed run completion (attached only when the sum needs it), and the anchored+local denouncement exemption; new selftest pins for each (including two that must KEEP failing: assert-wrong-after-negating-right, and asserted-wrong beside an accepted figure). v4 (same day, after live run 2): scorer-side only — sentence-scoped hedge detection (labelled roundings like 'Rounded alternatives … to 2 decimals … the exact version remains X' are honest rounding within approx_tolerance; hedge words NEVER rescue a figure hundreds of percent off — pinned by a fail-string), sentence-scoped denouncement windows, and approx/denouncement made orthogonal. New selftest pins for each. v5 (same day, rescore of run 2): scorer-side only — multiplication-expanded echo gaps ('4 crore (4 × 10,000,000) + 18 lakh …': gap digits may equal a component's coefficient, scaled value or unit multiplier; residue class gains × ( ) ) and markdown code-span backticks count as mark adjacency. A wrong-sum multiplication decomposition stays flagged (pinned fail-string). Case expectations and accepted values are UNCHANGED from v1/v2/v3/v4. v6 (same day, after live run 3): scorer-side only — currency-marked coefficients inside a TRUE product identity absorb into their product ('₹12 × 100,000 = 1,200,000' is the term 1,200,000 written expanded; its right-hand figure is an echo, not an independent claim), runs may complete across an echo gap, SI space grouping parses as one figure ('125 000 µg' = 0.125 g), and the whole mechanism is fail-closed: a FALSE identity absorbs nothing (pinned), an unlabelled rounded assertion still fails (pinned — this was a REAL live model defect, not a scorer gap), and merging never launders a 1000x error ('4 500 µg' pinned failing). v7 (same day, after live run 4): scorer-side only — a scale-word term restated as an equality identity in digits ('8 lakh = 800,000') is one term spelled twice: the digits are an echo of the same term (skipped as an independent claim) and the decomposition run may be a SINGLE scale component completed by its addend ('8 lakh … plus 120' = 800,120), attach still requiring the sum to equal an accepted value; fail-closed as always — a FALSE spelling ('8 lakh = 810,000') absorbs nothing, a TRUE spelling whose sum is wrong ('9 lakh = 900,000 plus 120 totals ₹800,120') stays flagged, and a lone wrong scale assertion ('8 lakh (= 800,000)' vs an accepted ₹8,00,120) keeps failing (three pinned fail-strings; the pass pins mirror live run 4's fully-true costs-line decomposition, which the v6 scorer wrongly flagged). v8 (same day, after live run 5): scorer-side only — two generality bugs fixed, both content-neutral: (1) suffix ADJACENCY — the figure-suffix regex no longer bridges a dash, so a section number before an em-dash next to a heading word ('Restatement 1 — crore') is no longer a phantom '1 crore' claim (same adjacency discipline the currency marks use); (2) gap-token word boundary on EVERY alternative — the boundary lookahead had attached to only the last alternative, chopping '4 crores 18 lakhs 25 thousand' gaps to residue 's', so exact-summing PLURAL place-value runs were never explained. Neither fix launders anything: wrong-sum plural decompositions (pinned in both A and C1) and adjacent wrong scale claims beside structure words (pinned in A) keep failing; the pass pins mirror live run 5's fully-true A and B answers, which the v7 scorer wrongly flagged. Case expectations and accepted values are UNCHANGED from v1/v2/v3/v4/v5/v6/v7.
